claims.statement: Budesonide MMX is preferred over systemic steroids for 5-ASA-refractory mild-moderate UC; systemic steroids are reserved for failure or severe disease

claims.statement: Oral 5-ASA ≥2 g/d and topical 5-ASA for distal disease are strongly recommended for maintenance despite very low-quality evidence; thiopurines are strongly recommended for steroid-dependent or 5-ASA-intolerant patients

claims.evidence_excerpt: Prednisone equivalent doses of 40-60 mg/day (or 1 mg/kg/day) are effective for inducing symptomatic response. claims.statement: Oral mesalamine should NOT be used for active Crohn's disease; sulfasalazine is effective only for colonic disease (R10-R11)
claims.evidence_excerpt: The negative recommendation against mesalamine is one of the strongest in the guideline. Despite widespread use, multiple meta-analyses show no consistent benefit of mesalamine over placebo for induction or mucosal healing. claims.evidence_excerpt: Pooled data from two RCTs (n=267): corticosteroids were twice as effective as placebo for clinical remission (RR 1.99; 95% CI 1.51-2.64).
